observationsNotFindings: The subject and the occupancy artifacts are untracked in git at review time. That is the correct state for a draft under review and for a CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED artifact pending a D-000 recording; the already-recorded siblings are tracked, which is consistent with recording being what commits an artifact. Not a defect and not charged.

The subject occupancy v2 carries reviewStatus 'AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW' even though its two Stage A verdicts now exist and both ACCEPT. This is an artefact of the file having been frozen at 0444 before its reviewers ran, and it matches how the recorded G26 sibling behaved. The draft does not reproduce or rely on that field, so nothing follows for this entry. Noted only so the custody trail is complete.

The draft reports Stage A for both reviewers but says nothing about Stage B, whereas the adopted D-226 entry reports both. That asymmetry is correct rather than an omission: Stage B for D-227 is this review and its counterpart, which do not exist in final form at draft time. The D-226 comparison is against an entry already carried through adoption.

Decision 2 attributes three closed obligations to leftover-join.v3 but does not name OBL-G27-EXECUTION or OBL-NT6-UNNAMED-REMAINDER-CLOSED, which are also leftoverDesign false at v3. The omission runs in the conservative direction — the draft claims fewer closures than the upstream would support — and both are handled in prose anyway, by the remainder-is-execution sentence and by the NT-6 unnamed-remainder negation. An under-claim cannot flip a leftoverDesign boolean, so this is not charged.

The remeasurement clause is self-limiting in a way worth noting favourably: it names the files whose movement forces re-measurement, exempts append-only COORD growth and heading hygiene as PASS-NO-SCOPE-EFFECT, and thereby states in the draft's own bytes the condition under which this CONSENT expires rather than leaving it to the reviewer.

A Codex counterpart file for this draft exists on disk at review time. I did not open it; its existence surfaced only as a filename while confirming my own write discipline. This verdict is therefore independent and unreconciled, and whether the two agree is not knowable from this file and is for the coordinator to determine.

summaryForCoordinator: CONSENT at 0 MUST-FIX and 0 SHOULD-FIX. I ran 27 attacks — the 21 the dispatch named plus six of my own on precedent drift, upstream staleness, lineage increment, the no-cell-edit branch, entry numbering, and live-token correspondence — and refuted all 27 against live bytes. All seven cited digests recompute identically; the subject is unmoved at adc02f50 and 0444; both occupancy v2 Stage A verdicts are 0444 and both parse as ACCEPT with empty blockers, mustFix and shouldFix. The load-bearing claims were tested from upstream bytes rather than the draft's summary of them: leftover-join.v3's six leftoverDesign booleans enumerated directly, leaving exactly [OBL-G27-FX-AUTHORING]; the input-corpus basis agreeing from both directions at g27-input-corpus.v1; naming v6 containing zero occurrences of DR-G27, so the D-153 parentage stands and the naming-v6 decoy is refused. The count the dispatch flagged is exact — Claude Stage A returned seven observationsNotFindings, all bare strings with no identifier field, and the draft records them as seven and unlabeled without inventing a single identifier, while Codex's own counters confirm zero advisories and zero observations. The non-unwrite span was set-differenced rather than eyeballed: exactly D-167 through D-226, 60 entries, D-168 and D-226 both present, no gap or duplicate. Every lineage token increments correctly from the adopted D-226 entry — D-152 to D-153, D-201 to D-202, after-D-225 to after-D-226, span to D-226, C-D226 to C-D227 — and the non-rewrite gate list is D-226's set plus G26 minus G27, exactly as the subject change requires. Every SATISFIED, QUALIFIED, Class A, required-now-26 and docs/v2/implementation string in the draft is negating or historical scoping, never a live claim. The gate-row obligation is met affirmatively: the draft states it does not claim D-056 gates 2 and 3 fail to hold. I found nothing to charge at either grade. Recommend recording, subject to the Codex counterpart and to the draft's own remeasurement clause.
